ruled: THE FIFTEEN DASHBOARD WHEN-RULES DAVE ACCEPTED ARE HIS WORDING NOW, EACH AS DRAFTED (plan lane 4d; R4a's `when-rules.proposed.json`). Per part, the page's sentence for the rule and his verdict, verbatim: 4c·1 Filter bar (`filter-toolbar-bar`): "Use it when two or more records need filtering or sorting. It sits only above the thing it drives, never on its own." — "Accept" · 4c·2 Footer (`footer`): "Every app page ends with the app footer, after the main area. Never inside the bento wall." — "Accept" · 4c·3 Dashboard bento template (`template-dashboard-bento`): "Use it when the page answers "how are things, and what needs me?" and is built on the bento. Borrow its grammar; choose every part from the graph. On a plain grid, the plain dashboard template takes over." — "Accept" · 4c·5 Button (`button`): "A button is for one action. When a main action has related actions beside it, the split button takes over." — "Accept" · 4c·7 Breadcrumbs (`breadcrumbs`): "The path of pages above this one, two or more deep. It answers "where am I?" and sits beside the main nav and tabs, not instead of them." — "Accept" · 4c·8 Bar chart (`chart-bar`): "Comparing categories. Over time, the line chart. Parts of a whole, the pie. Parts over time, the stacked area." — "Accept" · 4c·9 Page title (`headers`): "A page, screen or section title on its own. With actions or tabs beside it, the page-header lock-up takes over." — "Accept"; with his words, verbatim: "we have to work on this lock-up though" · 4c·10 KPI tile (`kpi-tile`): "One number with its change and a trend line. No trend line, the stat card. A target is the point, the bullet chart. Money against what is already scheduled, the runway bar." — "Accept" · 4c·11 Layout (`layout-utilities`): "Arranging blocks without drawing a surface. A bordered surface per item, cards. A row of 3 to 6 headline numbers, the stats band." — "Accept" · 4c·12 Legend (`legend`): "Only when two or more series are drawn. A lone chart keeps its key inside itself. A legend stands alone only when it keys several charts." — "Accept" · 4c·13 Main navigation (`navigations`): "The whole set of places to go. In the side-nav shell, the sidebar nav takes over. On a phone, the tab bar." — "Accept" · 4c·14 Stat card (`stat-card`): "One number with its change and no trend line. The default headline number." — "Accept" · 4c·15 Status dot (`status-indicator`): "One state, a dot and a label, up to 4 columns wide. Attached to something else, the badge." — "Accept" · 4c·16 Summary (`summary`): "Two or more name-and-value rows, 6 columns or wider. A cap being spent against, the meter. Inline, the badge." — "Accept" · 4c·17 View options (`view-options`): "Never. Replaced on 24 July; the view switch is the segmented control." — "Accept". ⬛ WHAT THE ACCEPTS TOOK: the page's recommendation, "accept all seventeen as drafted", on these fifteen — the drafted `when` of each row, which the page put to him in plain words (the plain words are lane B5's). With button it takes the one row the drafting lane added itself ("the one row that came from the lane, not from your words or the probe"); with the bento template it takes the `layout.grammar` field the row needs in knowledge/when-fields.json (not there at HEAD 01fb005a). At HEAD 01fb005a, 11 of the fifteen already read in their metas byte for byte as drafted (breadcrumbs, chart-bar, headers, kpi-tile, layout-utilities, legend, navigations, stat-card, status-indicator, summary, view-options); 4 were draft only there and are to be built (filter-toolbar-bar, footer, template-dashboard-bento, button) — lane B6 of this wave is building them, and the enacting commit stamps this ruling. ⛔ NOT IN THIS RULING: the list rule (4c·4, `list-items`) and the top-nav shell rule (4c·6, `app-shell-top-nav`) — he answered "Change" on both; each is its own open thread (W-305e1, W-305e2) and neither draft is accepted. The page-title lock-up he wants worked on is open thread W-305e3; his accept of the page-title rule stands.
